dev.status.bridge.already_on.text: the device is already on the bridge
dev.status.bridge.already_on.note: Status the device's root helper writes when the owner asks to switch the bridge on (Settings > Bridge) and the device already uses it. The bridge is off-the.cloud, the relay that makes the device reachable from outside the home.

dev.status.bridge.claim_failed.note: Error under the name field when switching the bridge on from Settings: the bridge refused the name the owner chose and gave no reason.

dev.status.bridge.claim_unavailable.text: could not reserve that name right now
dev.status.bridge.claim_unavailable.note: Error under the name field when switching the bridge on from Settings: the bridge could not reserve the name just now (its own error, try again later).

dev.status.bridge.config_missing.note: Error shown in Settings > Bridge when switching the bridge on or off failed: the device's configuration file was not found. {path} is that file's path, such as /etc/otc_prod.ini.

dev.status.bridge.config_update_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Bridge when switching the bridge on or off failed: the device's configuration file could not be changed. {path} is that file's path, such as /etc/otc_prod.ini.

dev.status.bridge.email_not_verified.text: Confirm your email first: we sent a link to {email}. Open it, then sign in here again to continue.
dev.status.bridge.email_not_verified.note: Error shown when signing in to an Off The Cloud account from Settings > Bridge (to switch the bridge on) with an account whose email address isn't confirmed yet. {email} is the account's email address; the bridge has just sent it a confirmation link.

dev.status.bridge.invalid_credentials.text: wrong email or password - if you signed up with Google or Apple, use that instead (on the account page, then a setup code)
dev.status.bridge.invalid_credentials.note: Error shown when signing in to an Off The Cloud account from Settings > Bridge with an email and password the bridge doesn't accept. Accounts made with Google or Apple have no password: those get a setup code from the account page (off-the.cloud/account) and type it here instead.

dev.status.bridge.invalid_name.note: Error under the name field when switching the bridge on from Settings: the bridge doesn't allow that name (reserved, or not a valid name).

dev.status.bridge.invalid_setup_code.text: that setup code is not valid or has expired
dev.status.bridge.invalid_setup_code.note: Error shown in Settings > Bridge when the setup code typed (an 8-character code from the account page, valid for 15 minutes) is wrong or too old.

dev.status.bridge.login_required.text: sign in to register a name
dev.status.bridge.login_required.note: Error under the name field when switching the bridge on from Settings: the account sign-in behind the request was not accepted (it may have expired), so the name can't be registered.

dev.status.bridge.name_held.text: that name was released recently and is held for its previous owner for 30 days
dev.status.bridge.name_held.note: Error under the name field when switching the bridge on from Settings: someone gave this name up recently, and it stays reserved for them for 30 days.

dev.status.bridge.name_rule.text: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens only
dev.status.bridge.name_rule.note: Error under the name field when switching the bridge on from Settings: the device's name (it becomes name.off-the.cloud) may only hold lower-case letters a to z, digits and hyphens.

dev.status.bridge.name_taken.note: Error under the name field when switching the bridge on from Settings: another device already uses this name.

dev.status.bridge.needs_update.text: this device needs updating before it can join the bridge: Settings → Update
dev.status.bridge.needs_update.note: Error shown when switching the bridge on (or leaving it) from Settings on a device whose software is too old to do it: install the update first. Settings → Update names the Settings screen and its Update button; keep the arrow.

dev.status.bridge.no_name.text: no name on {bridge} has been reserved for this device
dev.status.bridge.no_name.note: Error shown in Settings > Bridge when the device's root helper couldn't switch the bridge on: no name was reserved for the device first. {bridge} is the bridge's address, such as off-the.cloud.

dev.status.bridge.not_host_name.text: the configured bridge ({bridge}) is not a host name
dev.status.bridge.not_host_name.note: Error shown in Settings > Bridge when switching the bridge on failed: the bridge address in the device's configuration is not a valid host name. {bridge} is that address as configured.

dev.status.bridge.on_bridge.text: The device is on the bridge as {domain}
dev.status.bridge.on_bridge.note: Status the device's root helper writes once it has switched the bridge on, just before the device restarts to use it. {domain} is the device's new address on the bridge, such as mydevice.off-the.cloud.

dev.status.bridge.setup_unavailable.note: Error shown when signing in to an Off The Cloud account from Settings > Bridge: the sign-in worked, but the bridge could not issue the code that lets the device register its name (its own error, try again).

dev.status.bridge.signin_failed.note: Error shown when signing in to an Off The Cloud account from Settings > Bridge failed and the bridge gave no reason.

dev.status.bridge.signin_first.text: sign in to your Off The Cloud account first
dev.status.bridge.signin_first.note: Error shown when switching the bridge on from Settings without having signed in to an Off The Cloud account first.

dev.status.bridge.signin_unavailable.text: could not sign in right now
dev.status.bridge.signin_unavailable.note: Error shown when signing in to an Off The Cloud account from Settings > Bridge: the bridge could not check the sign-in just now (its own error, try again later).

dev.status.bridge.switch_off_failed.note: Error shown when the device could not ask its root helper to take it off the bridge (Settings > Bridge, Leave the bridge). {detail} is the system's own error, in English, such as permission denied.

dev.status.bridge.switch_on_failed.note: Error shown when the device could not ask its root helper to switch the bridge on (Settings > Bridge). {detail} is the system's own error, in English, such as permission denied.

dev.status.bridge.switching_off.note: Status the device's root helper writes while it takes the device off the bridge, before the device restarts.

dev.status.bridge.switching_on.note: Status the device's root helper writes while it switches the bridge on, before the device restarts.

dev.status.bridge.terms_not_accepted.text: accept the terms of use first: sign in at off-the.cloud/account and accept them there
dev.status.bridge.terms_not_accepted.note: Error shown when signing in to an Off The Cloud account from Settings > Bridge with an account that hasn't accepted the current terms of use. off-the.cloud/account is the account page's address; keep it as it is.

dev.status.bridge.too_many_attempts.text: too many failed attempts, try again later
dev.status.bridge.too_many_attempts.note: Error shown when signing in to an Off The Cloud account from Settings > Bridge after too many wrong passwords from this address: the bridge refuses for a while.

dev.status.bridge.too_many_claims.text: please wait a moment before trying another name
dev.status.bridge.too_many_claims.note: Error under the name field when switching the bridge on from Settings: names were tried too quickly, the bridge asks to wait a little.

dev.status.bridge.unreachable.note: Error shown in Settings > Bridge when the device could not connect to the bridge. {bridge} is the bridge's address, such as off-the.cloud; {detail} is the system's own network error, in English.

dev.status.raid.degraded.text: RAID array degraded: only {active} of {total} disks active
dev.status.raid.degraded.note: Warning shown in every app's device status while the storage mirror (two disks, each holding a copy of every file) is missing a disk. {active} is the number of disks working, {total} the number the mirror has (2).

dev.status.raid.degraded_bottom.text: RAID array degraded: only {active} of {total} disks active - the disk in the bottom blue USB port stopped working
dev.status.raid.degraded_bottom.note: Warning shown in every app's device status while the storage mirror (two disks, each holding a copy of every file) is missing a disk, naming it: the device has two blue USB ports, one above the other, and the disk in the bottom one stopped working. {active} is the number of disks working, {total} the number the mirror has (2).

dev.status.raid.degraded_top.text: RAID array degraded: only {active} of {total} disks active - the disk in the top blue USB port stopped working
dev.status.raid.degraded_top.note: Warning shown in every app's device status while the storage mirror (two disks, each holding a copy of every file) is missing a disk, naming it: the device has two blue USB ports, one above the other, and the disk in the top one stopped working. {active} is the number of disks working, {total} the number the mirror has (2).

dev.status.raid.degraded_unknown.text: RAID array degraded: only {active} of {total} disks active - one of the two storage disks stopped working
dev.status.raid.degraded_unknown.note: Warning shown in every app's device status while the storage mirror (two disks, each holding a copy of every file) is missing a disk the device can't place in a USB port. {active} is the number of disks working, {total} the number the mirror has (2).

dev.status.raid.degraded_working_bottom.text: RAID array degraded: only {active} of {total} disks active - the disk in the bottom blue USB port still works, the other one stopped working
dev.status.raid.degraded_working_bottom.note: Warning shown in every app's device status while the storage mirror (two disks, each holding a copy of every file) is missing a disk and the device can't tell which one stopped, but can tell which still works: the device has two blue USB ports, one above the other, and the disk in the bottom one still works. {active} is the number of disks working, {total} the number the mirror has (2).

dev.status.raid.degraded_working_top.text: RAID array degraded: only {active} of {total} disks active - the disk in the top blue USB port still works, the other one stopped working
dev.status.raid.degraded_working_top.note: Warning shown in every app's device status while the storage mirror (two disks, each holding a copy of every file) is missing a disk and the device can't tell which one stopped, but can tell which still works: the device has two blue USB ports, one above the other, and the disk in the top one still works. {active} is the number of disks working, {total} the number the mirror has (2).

dev.status.tailscale.cli_missing.text: tailscale is not installed on this device
dev.status.tailscale.cli_missing.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when turning it on or off: the tailscale program is missing from the device. tailscale (lower case) is the program's name.

dev.status.tailscale.disable_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when turning it off failed. Funnel is Tailscale's feature that publishes the device on the internet. {detail} is the tailscale program's own error, in English.

dev.status.tailscale.enable_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when turning it on failed. Funnel is Tailscale's feature that publishes the device on the internet. {detail} is the tailscale program's own error, in English.

dev.status.tailscale.join_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when the device could not join the owner's tailnet (their private Tailscale network). {detail} is the tailscale program's own error, in English.

dev.status.tailscale.not_installed.text: Tailscale is not installed on this device
dev.status.tailscale.not_installed.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when the device's root helper could not start Tailscale because it isn't installed.

dev.status.tailscale.operator_failed.text: tailscaled started, but the device could not be made its operator
dev.status.tailscale.operator_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel: the Tailscale service (tailscaled, the program's name) started, but the device's own service was not allowed to control it.

dev.status.tailscale.request_off_failed.text: could not ask for Tailscale to be switched off: {detail}
dev.status.tailscale.request_off_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when turning it off: the device could not ask its root helper to stop the Tailscale service. {detail} is the system's own error, in English.

dev.status.tailscale.request_on_failed.text: could not ask for Tailscale to be switched on: {detail}
dev.status.tailscale.request_on_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when turning it on: the device could not ask its root helper to start the Tailscale service. {detail} is the system's own error, in English.

dev.status.tailscale.start_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel: the device's root helper could not start the Tailscale service. tailscaled is the program's name.

dev.status.tailscale.timeout_off.text: Tailscale did not switch off in time - try again
dev.status.tailscale.timeout_off.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when turning it off: the Tailscale service did not stop within 45 seconds.

dev.status.tailscale.timeout_on.text: Tailscale did not switch on in time - try again
dev.status.tailscale.timeout_on.note: Error shown in Settings > Tailscale Funnel when turning it on: the Tailscale service did not start within 45 seconds.

dev.status.tailscale.unknown_request.note: Error the device's Tailscale root helper writes when it was asked for something other than switching Tailscale on or off (it should never happen).

dev.status.wifi.no_connection.text: the device has no network connection to restart
dev.status.wifi.no_connection.note: Why the device's Wi-Fi restart (its watchdog restarts a Wi-Fi that has become very slow) didn't happen: the device has no network connection at all. Shown inside an alert in Alerts.

dev.status.wifi.not_wifi.text: the device isn't connected over Wi-Fi
dev.status.wifi.not_wifi.note: Why the device's Wi-Fi restart didn't happen: the device is connected another way (an Ethernet cable). Shown inside an alert in Alerts.

dev.status.wifi.rebooted.text: The Wi-Fi did not reconnect after its restart, so the device restarted
dev.status.wifi.rebooted.note: What the device's Wi-Fi restart did: the Wi-Fi did not come back, so the whole device was restarted.

dev.status.wifi.restarted.note: What the device's Wi-Fi restart did: the Wi-Fi was restarted and is connected again.

dev.status.wifi.restarting.note: Status while the device restarts its Wi-Fi (its watchdog restarts a Wi-Fi that has become very slow).

dev.status.wifi.too_soon.text: the Wi-Fi was restarted less than 30 minutes ago
dev.status.wifi.too_soon.note: Why the device's Wi-Fi restart didn't happen: it restarts the Wi-Fi at most once every 30 minutes. Shown inside an alert in Alerts.
